Plot GO enrichment results

Source: R/easyGOPlot.R
easyGOPlot.Rd

Plots the most significant GO terms from easytopGO() or a VEuPathDB enrichment table. Input p-values are sorted before selecting the top terms. Redundant rows are identified using GO.ID when available, otherwise the term description; this is a display-only reduction, not a change to enrichment.

Usage

easyGOPlot(
  res,
  title = "GO Biological processes",
  limit = 20L,
  desc = "Term",
  genecounts = "Significant",
  sortby = NULL,
  min_genes = NULL
)

Arguments

res

A data.frame of GO enrichment results.

title

Plot title.

limit

Maximum number of terms to display (positive integer).

desc

Name of the term-description column (e.g. "Term" or "Name").

genecounts

Name of the gene-count column (e.g. "Significant" or "Result count"). For KS, Significant may refer to a nominal gene cutoff.

sortby

Name of a numeric GO p-value column. When NULL (default), uses the first available among padj, fisher, ks, P-value and p-value.

min_genes

Optional minimum count for plotting (NULL means no filter). Applied only to the displayed terms, not before GO enrichment/FDR testing.

Value

A ggplot2 object. Empty results produce a labelled empty plot.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
gores <- easytopGO(
  geneID = down_padj, bkggset = background,
  gaf = "annotation.gaf.gz", useBiomart = FALSE,
  useGAF = TRUE, stats = "fisher"
)
easyGOPlot(gores, sortby = "fisher", min_genes = 3)
# For KS output:
# easyGOPlot(ks_result, sortby = "ks")
# For a VEuPathDB result with numeric p-values:
# easyGOPlot(veupath, desc = "Name", genecounts = "Result count",
#            sortby = "P-value")
} # }
